sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report documents confirmed unauthorized financial transactions impacting cardholder C13487 on payment instrument C13487-K1. The suspicious activity occurred on or around 2016-11-22 via the online channel under transaction identifier 3478561 totaling $74.96 USD. Investigation by the bank's automated fraud intelligence system identified an anomalous transaction profile classified under the 'undocumented' typology. The originating transactions were initiated through a device profile characterized as 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' with connection parameters inconsistent with historical cardholder baselines. Multi-hop graph traversal revealed that this identical digital fingerprint was simultaneously utilized across 51 other distinct customer payment cards (C00255-K1, C01289-K2), establishing an organized cross-account credential harvesting ring. Upon controlled direct verification by fraud operations, the cardholder confirmed that they remained in physical custody of the plastic card but explicitly denied initiating or authorizing the aforementioned debits. Analysis of network metadata and transaction velocity patterns indicates that unauthorized credentials were electronically obtained and leveraged for testing or unauthorized extraction. In accordance with Bank Fraud Policy v1.0 and regulatory guidance, payment card C13487-K1 was immediately placed under administrative block to mitigate ongoing financial exposure. All secondary accounts linked through the shared device cluster have been placed under heightened fraud surveillance, and total cumulative exposure has been contained to $74.96 USD. This filing is submitted pursuant to BSA/AML reporting requirements to notify authorities of potential cyber-enabled payment fraud and synthetic or compromised credential abuse.
